chains.title: T allele creates an activating CEBPA-dependent SORT1 enhancer
chains.element: The variant lies in a liver-active regulatory element whose activity is increased by CEBPA binding.

links.claim: The alt T allele is expected to bind CEBPA more strongly; CEBPA is favored over related C/EBP factors because it is the TF associated with the established rs12740374 mechanism. No QBiC-SELEX result or model status is available in the supplied case.
The variant is in a regulatory element that can act as a liver enhancer, and stronger CEBPA binding on T is expected to increase its activity.
The regulatory effect occurs primarily in hepatocytes.
Increased hepatic SORT1 lowers circulating LDL cholesterol and is expected to reduce myocardial-infarction risk.

predictions: In heterozygous hepatocytes, CEBPA occupancy at the variant should be greater on T than G.
Replacing G with T should increase SORT1 expression and reduce a measure of hepatic lipoprotein output.
falsified_if: There is no reproducible T-biased CEBPA occupancy in an appropriate hepatocyte context.
An endogenous G-to-T edit does not increase SORT1 expression.

chains.title: A related C/EBP factor, CEBPB, mediates the enhancer effect
chains.element: The variant is in a liver-active regulatory element whose activity is increased by CEBPB binding.

links.claim: The alt T allele is hypothesized to bind CEBPB more strongly; this is a competing possibility because related C/EBP factors can recognize similar sequences, but no QBiC-SELEX result or model status is available here.
The variant-containing element acts as a liver enhancer when occupied by CEBPB.
The regulatory effect occurs primarily in hepatocytes.
Increased hepatic SORT1 lowers circulating LDL cholesterol and is expected to reduce myocardial-infarction risk.

predictions: In heterozygous hepatocytes, CEBPB occupancy should be greater on T than G and more informative than CEBPA occupancy.
Reducing CEBPB should weaken the T-allele effect on SORT1 expression.
falsified_if: CEBPB shows no T-biased occupancy while CEBPA shows clear T-biased occupancy.
Reducing CEBPB does not alter the allele-dependent SORT1 response.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs12740374
predictions: The variant will not show a reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy or endogenous regulatory effect; the association could reflect linkage or another explanation.
falsified_if: An endogenous allele swap produces a reproducible, allele-dependent TF occupancy change and corresponding expression change.

chains.title: CEBPA binds the T allele but represses SORT1
chains.element: The variant-containing regulatory element acts as a CEBPA-dependent repressor of SORT1.

links.claim: The alt T allele is hypothesized to bind CEBPA more strongly; no QBiC-SELEX result or model status is available in the supplied case.
At this element, increased CEBPA binding is hypothesized to reduce rather than increase regulatory activity.
The repressive element lowers SORT1 expression.
The regulatory effect occurs primarily in hepatocytes.
Lower hepatic SORT1 is hypothesized to raise LDL cholesterol and myocardial-infarction risk.

predictions: T should show greater CEBPA occupancy than G, but endogenous T should reduce SORT1 expression.
A G-to-T edit should increase LDL-related lipoprotein output, opposite to H1.
falsified_if: A G-to-T edit increases SORT1 expression in hepatocytes.
The T allele does not show greater CEBPA occupancy in an appropriate hepatocyte context.

matrix.test: Allele-specific CUT&RUN-qPCR for CEBPA and CEBPB at the variant in heterozygous hepatocytes

outcomes.outcome: T-biased CEBPA occupancy, stronger than any T-biased CEBPB signal.
T-biased CEBPB occupancy, stronger than any T-biased CEBPA signal.
T-biased CEBPA occupancy; occupancy alone does not establish whether CEBPA activates or represses.
No reproducible allele-specific occupancy for either factor.

matrix.test: Endogenous G-to-T allele swap in a hepatocyte model followed by SORT1 expression measurement

outcomes.outcome: SORT1 expression increases, with the response dependent on CEBPB.

next_experiment: Perform allele-specific CUT&RUN-qPCR for CEBPA and CEBPB at rs12740374 in heterozygous hepatocytes. It is the cheapest proposed test that distinguishes the leading CEBPA chain from the CEBPB alternative.
